title: Idempotency keys are a GLOBAL unique with no production writer — a client key collision resolves tenant B's retry to tenant A's approval (REVIEW-FINDINGS #7)
why_open: apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:466 declares `idempotencyKey String? @unique` on ApprovalRequest — one unique index across every tenant, created as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "ApprovalRequest_idempotencyKey_key" ON "ApprovalRequest"("idempotencyKey")` at apps/web/prisma/migrations/20260730000000_baseline/migration.sql:740. ApprovalRequest is classified TENANT_SCOPED (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:38), so a client-supplied key is a cross-tenant handle. The port contract already disagrees with the schema: apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:37-44 declares `claimIdempotency({ key, tenantId, requestDigest, expiresAt })` and bus.ts:118-123/169/188/200/206/219 threads `context.tenantId` through every call — so any Prisma implementation of that port over the current column either drops the tenant (leak) or gets a unique violation from another tenant's row (denial of service). Nothing writes the column today: grep across apps/web/src finds `idempotencyKey` only in bus.ts, bus.test.ts and the reminders job envelope (apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts:63) — `dispatch()` in bus.ts has ZERO production callers, so the whole typed-command path (parse, claim, re-authorize, expectedVersion) is unreachable. Note: tools/loop/harvested-queue.json GE-021-004 proposes wiring dispatch using "the EXISTING unique column ... so no new table or migration is needed" — that advice would cement the leak, and this item must land the migration first or be serialized with it. Registry status FAIL; ledger docs/implementation/payments-treasury-execution-ledger.md marks PAY-140-005 FAIL/imported.
smallest_real_change: 1) Migration: `DROP INDEX "ApprovalRequest_idempotencyKey_key"; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "ApprovalRequest_institutionId_idempotencyKey_key" ON "ApprovalRequest"("institutionId","idempotencyKey");` and change schema.prisma:466 to `idempotencyKey String?` with `@@unique([institutionId, idempotencyKey])` beside the existing @@index block at :475-476. 2) Add apps/web/src/lib/commands/prisma-ports.ts implementing CommandPorts against Prisma: `claimIdempotency` does a conditional `updateMany({ where: { institutionId: input.tenantId, id: resourceId, idempotencyKey: null }, data: { idempotencyKey: input.key } })` and on count 0 reads back `findFirst({ where: { institutionId: input.tenantId, idempotencyKey: input.key } })` to build the IdempotencyRecord; `authorize` calls the same availableActions/borrowed-authority path actOnApproval already uses; `currentVersion` reads the approval. 3) Route apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:actOnApproval (the transaction at :391) through `dispatch(...)` so the port has a real caller. Test (apps/web/src/lib/commands/prisma-ports.itest.ts against the running Postgres, plus a fake-port unit test in bus.test.ts): two institutions each submit the SAME client key; assert both claims succeed and each resolves to its own approval id, and that a repeat of tenant A's key replays A's stored result and never returns B's. MUTATION TO PROVE: delete `institutionId` from the `where` in claimIdempotency (i.e. restore the global-key behaviour) and confirm the cross-tenant test FAILS with tenant B resolving to tenant A's approval; restore and confirm green. Second mutation: revert the migration to the global unique and confirm `prisma migrate deploy` + the itest reds on a unique violation.

title: The payment subledger is not immutable — a posted LedgerEntry is hard-deleted, and LedgerEntry is absent from APPEND_ONLY_MODELS
why_open: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:295-317 `deleteLedgerEntry` calls `tx.ledgerEntry.delete({ where: { id: entry.id } })` at :307 and then recomputes BudgetLine.actualCents — so a posted spend, with its approval / vendor / receipt links, disappears without trace. The one control that could refuse it does not cover the model: apps/web/src/lib/audit-append-only.ts:64 is `export const APPEND_ONLY_MODELS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["AuditEvent"])`, and its own header says the next append-only table 'should be one line here'. LedgerEntry is TENANT_SCOPED via `Organization.institutionId` (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:105) and apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/scope-args.ts permits delete on it. The model itself carries no versioning or reversal linkage — apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:820-847 has no `reversalOfId`, no `postedAt` distinct from `occurredAt`, and no `schemaVersion` on the accounting event, so 'versioned accounting-event contracts' has nothing behind it either. The auto-post path has the same shape: apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:347 creates the SPEND entry with no immutability guarantee.
smallest_real_change: 1) Add `"LedgerEntry"` to APPEND_ONLY_MODELS at apps/web/src/lib/audit-append-only.ts:64 (the extension at :113 already refuses every non-allowed operation on a listed model, so no new machinery). 2) Migration + schema.prisma: add `reversalOfId String?` with a self-relation and `postedAt DateTime @default(now())` and `eventVersion Int @default(1)` to LedgerEntry. 3) Replace the body of `deleteLedgerEntry` (finance/actions.ts:295) with `reverseLedgerEntry`: read the entry, create a NEW entry with `amountCents: -entry.amountCents`, `kind: "ADJUSTMENT"`, `reversalOfId: entry.id`, a required reason in `memo`, then recompute actualCents from the aggregate exactly as it does now. Add a pure `reversalOf(entry)` helper to apps/web/src/lib/finance.ts beside `ledgerSignedCents` (:257) so the sign rule has one home, and update the LedgerDrawer delete control (apps/web/src/components/finance/LedgerDrawer.tsx) to say 'Reverse'. TEST (apps/web/src/lib/audit-append-only.test.ts): drive the real Prisma extension with model 'LedgerEntry' and operation 'delete' and assert it throws AuditAppendOnlyError; plus a finance.test.ts case asserting `reversalOf` produces the exact negation and that summing entry + reversal is zero. MUTATION TO PROVE: remove `"LedgerEntry"` from APPEND_ONLY_MODELS and confirm the extension test FAILS (the delete is permitted); restore. Second mutation: change `-entry.amountCents` to `entry.amountCents` and confirm the sum-to-zero test reds.

title: Nothing prevents a posting that exceeds the approved allocation — the over-budget check is a rendered warning only
why_open: The remaining allocation is computed and DISPLAYED but never enforced. apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/[id]/page.tsx:118-124 computes `lineRemaining = bl.budgetedCents - bl.actualCents`, and :245-249 renders a warning when `reimb.amountCents > lineRemaining` — an approver reads it and can approve anyway. On the server side, apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:330-377 auto-posts the SPEND on final approval after checking only (a) that no entry already carries this approvalId and (b) that the budget line exists — there is no comparison against `budgetedCents` at all. The manual path is the same: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:219-289 `postLedgerEntry` validates the line belongs to the org, parses the amount and writes, with no cap check. `Budget.allocatedCents` and `Budget.totalCents` (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:718-735) are written by apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:950-963 and read by nothing that refuses a spend. So 'prevent transfers exceeding eligible balance or approved allocation' has no code path anywhere.
smallest_real_change: Add a pure decision function to apps/web/src/lib/finance.ts beside `ledgerSignedCents` (:257): `export type AllocationVerdict = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string; remainingCents: number; requestedCents: number }` and `export function withinAllocation(input: { budgetedCents: number; actualCents: number; signedCents: number; overCommitAllowed: boolean }): AllocationVerdict` — integer cents throughout, refusing when `signedCents > 0 && actualCents + signedCents > budgetedCents` and `!overCommitAllowed`; a REIMBURSEMENT (negative) is always allowed because it lowers actual. Then call it at BOTH producers, inside the transaction, on values read in that transaction: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:262 (select budgetedCents/actualCents on the line at :225 and throw the verdict's reason) and apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:346 (extend the `db.budgetLine.findFirst` select at :339 to include budgetedCents/actualCents and refuse the approval decision rather than posting an over-allocation SPEND). Change the page.tsx:245 warning text to say the approval will be refused, so the UI and the server agree. TEST (apps/web/src/lib/finance.test.ts): a table over exactly-at-limit, one cent over, a negative reimbursement over the limit, and overCommitAllowed=true. MUTATION TO PROVE: flip the comparison in `withinAllocation` from `>` to `>=` and confirm the exactly-at-limit case reds; then delete the `withinAllocation` call from approvals/actions.ts:346 and confirm the producer-level test (an approval whose reimbursement exceeds the line is refused and no LedgerEntry row is written) reds — assert on the absence of the row, not on the helper's return value.

title: External and client-supplied IDs are globally unique across tenants, and no guard stops the next one being added
why_open: Five unique indexes on tenant-scoped models are declared globally rather than qualified by tenant (and by provider/mode/account where an external system supplies the value): apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:466 `idempotencyKey String? @unique` (client-supplied — the REVIEW-FINDINGS #7 leak), :1096 `eventId String @unique` on OutboxEvent, :301 `key String @unique` on Deliverable, :271 `positionCode String? @unique` on Seat, :353 `email String @unique` on DirectoryPerson. All five models are in the tenant-scoped registry (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:28,38,105 and neighbours). There is also no external-reference table at all: the only `provider` column in the schema is NextAuth's `Account.provider` (:35), so nothing records provider/mode/account alongside an external id. And there is no guard: `ls tests/security` shows 27 architecture guards and none of them reads the Prisma schema for unique scoping — the nearest neighbour, tests/security/email-is-not-a-key.test.mjs, checks call sites, not indexes. So the sixth global unique will be added exactly the way the first five were.
smallest_real_change: Add tests/security/external-ids-are-tenant-qualified.test.mjs, modelled line-for-line on tests/security/email-is-not-a-key.test.mjs (same node:test + fs schema-reading shape): parse apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma, and for every model whose name appears in the TENANT_SCOPED / reachable maps of apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts, assert that no field-level `@unique` exists on a column carrying an externally-supplied or client-supplied value — enforced as an explicit ALLOWED set (a short, named, commented list of the tenant-blind columns that may legitimately be global, e.g. Institution.slug) plus a REFUSED set naming the five above with the reason each is a cross-tenant handle. Ratchet: the test starts by asserting the count of unqualified uniques equals a constant and that constant may only shrink, the same shape tests/architecture/document-graph.test.mjs uses. Land the composite unique for ApprovalRequest.idempotencyKey with PAY-140-005 (same migration) so the guard starts with one already fixed and four named. MUTATION TO PROVE: add a `externalRef String @unique` field to a tenant-scoped model in schema.prisma and confirm the new guard reds naming that model; remove it and confirm green. Second mutation: move ApprovalRequest.idempotencyKey back to a bare `@unique` and confirm the count assertion reds.

title: No payments capability registry exists, and no capability or configuration option a tenant picks carries a price (NEXT-SESSION §7)
why_open: The catalog machinery is real — packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts has lifecycle (:55), effective-dated certification (:107), usability (:393) and scoped availability decisions (:552-601) — but it contains no payments entry: packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:659 `CATALOG_ENTRIES = [RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR, ...MODEL_CATALOG]`. Its scope axes are also narrower than the Bible §5 text quoted in its own header (tenant/environment/legal entity/population/country/region/provider/mode/version): `AvailabilityContext` at :529-537 carries only engineVersion, region, partition, marketplaceEnabled, now. Separately, NEXT-SESSION §7 is unmet everywhere: `CatalogEntry` (:151) and `CatalogRestrictions` (:128) have no price field; packages/provisioning/src/commercial.ts:62-79 prices a whole PLAN (`monthlyPriceCents`) and not an option; packages/configuration/src/definition.ts:24-66 `ConfigDefinition` has key/owner/type/default/allowedScopes/mergeStrategy/sensitivity/overridable/requiresCapability/description and no price; apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/new/ComposeForm.tsx:15-21 `ComposeAxis` values are {id,label,description} with no price and the form shows no running total. Grep for price/perSeat across packages/configuration and packages/platform-config returns only `formatMoney` (packages/platform-config/src/money.ts:35). So a tenant picks options through the whole composer without ever seeing what any of it costs.
smallest_real_change: 1) Add packages/finops/src/pricing.ts (exported from packages/finops/src/index.ts alongside the money exports at :10-24): `export interface OptionPrice { perSeat: Money; perOrganization: Money }` and `export function quoteOptions(options: readonly { key: string; price: OptionPrice }[], seats: number): { lines: readonly { key: string; perSeat: Money; seatTotal: Money; perOrganization: Money; lineTotal: Money }[]; runningTotal: Money }` — integer minor units via the existing `money`/`add`/`sum`, explicit currency, CurrencyMismatchError on a mixed quote. Quoting only; no movement. 2) Make the price REQUIRED on the option model: add `price: OptionPrice` to `CatalogEntry` (packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:151) and have `validatePackage`/a new `validateCatalogEntry` return a CatalogProblem when it is missing — a required field, so `tsc` catches every construction site, of which there are exactly two in production (RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR at :631 and MODEL_CATALOG in packages/platform-config/src/model-entry.ts) plus the fixtures in catalogs.test.ts. 3) Add the first payments capability entries to CATALOG_ENTRIES (:659) — e.g. `tenure.payments.control-plane` — lifecycle DRAFT with NO certification record, so `isUsable` refuses them `uncertified` exactly as the Relay connector is refused today; nothing is claimed available. 4) Carry the quote to the surface: the only production caller of `availabilityDecisions` is apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:71, and the composer is apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/new/ComposeForm.tsx — render per-seat, per-organisation and the running total beside each option, keeping e2e/layout.spec.ts colours. TEST (packages/finops/src/finops.test.ts + packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.test.ts): quote three options at 250 seats and assert the running total to the exact minor unit; assert `validateCatalogEntry` reports a problem for an entry with no price. MUTATION TO PROVE §7: delete the `price` from one entry in CATALOG_ENTRIES and confirm the catalog validation test reds; delete the `perSeat` line from `quoteOptions` and confirm the total test reds. Assert on what the page/composer emits, not on `quoteOptions` called directly, so the check survives the caller dropping it.

title: Financial figures carry an as-of time but no source citation — the operator cannot see which system a number came from
why_open: Half the requirement is built and half is absent. packages/finops/src/reporting.ts:27-50 `Figure` is `{ amount, kind, asOf, periodCompleteness }` and `figure()` refuses an unparseable asOf at :47, and `freshness()` at :68 flags staleness — that is the as-of half, and it is real. There is no source field anywhere: grep for `source` in packages/finops/src returns only the allocation driver naming, and the rendered surface says only 'as of {asOf}' (apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/cost/page.tsx:145-152) with no statement of which system produced the number. That matters most in exactly the place the module already worries about: apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-source.ts distinguishes CONNECTED from NOT_CONFIGURED precisely so a figure is never invented, and then the Figure it hands to the page cannot say it came from CUR rather than from an estimate. For payment status, balances and fees the same type is the intended carrier and it cannot cite a provider, an API version or a webhook.
smallest_real_change: Add a REQUIRED `source` to `Figure` — `export interface FigureSource { system: string; reference: string; retrievedAt: string }` — and make `figure(amount, kind, asOf, source, periodCompleteness?)` validate it the way it already validates asOf at reporting.ts:47 (empty system or reference throws, retrievedAt must parse). Required, not optional, so `tsc` names every construction site rather than letting a caller omit it silently. The construction sites, all of them, are inside this package plus one app: reporting.ts:286 (`summarize`), :89 (`forecastPeriod`, which must propagate the actual's source and mark it derived), :385 (`fleetCost`), and the single production entry point apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-source.ts:83 which passes `{ system: 'aws-cur', reference: `s3://${bucket}/${prefix}`, retrievedAt: asOf }` on the CONNECTED arm — the NOT_CONFIGURED arm builds no figure, so there is nothing to fake. Then render it at apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/cost/page.tsx:145 beside the existing 'as of' badge. TEST (packages/finops/src/finops.test.ts): `figure(...)` throws for a blank system and for an unparseable retrievedAt; `summarize(...)` propagates the same source onto actual, amortized and forecast. MUTATION TO PROVE: drop the `source` from the object `summarize` returns for `actual` and confirm the propagation test reds; then blank the `system` string at cost-source.ts:83 and confirm the page-level assertion (the rendered citation is non-empty) reds — assert on what the page emits, not on `figure()` called directly.

title: Maker-checker and conflict/recusal refusals are unreachable from production — the caller passes an empty world and never names the preparer
why_open: Self-approval and delegated authority ARE wired and correct: apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts:85-95 calls `mayDecide` and :118 gates both approval roles on it, and delegation runs through apps/web/src/lib/delegation.ts + `mayBorrowAuthority` (apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:4,228-238). The other three arms are dead. apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts:61 declares `const NO_STANDING_DECLARATIONS: ControlWorld = {}` and passes it on every call, so the DECLARED_CONFLICT / RECUSED / INCOMPATIBLE_DUTIES branches that `ControlWorld` feeds (packages/authorization/src/controls.ts:101-107) can never fire — the file's own comment says so, honestly: 'the schema has no ConflictDeclaration and no Recusal model'. And the `DecisionUnderReview` built at approvals.ts:87-93 supplies only resourceId/tenantId/raisedByPrincipalId, never `preparedByPrincipalId`, so the SAME_MAKER refusal at packages/authorization/src/controls.ts:130-140 — the actual maker-checker control this requirement names — is unreachable for every request in the product. apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma has no ConflictDeclaration and no Recusal model (models listed at 19-1088).
smallest_real_change: Start with the half that needs no new table: add `preparedById String?` to ApprovalRequest (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:455-477, plus migration), set it in the create path in apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/new (whoever drafted, when that is not the submitter — e.g. a treasurer preparing a president's request), carry it on `ApprovalView` (apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts:37-50) as a REQUIRED field so every producer of that view must answer, and pass it as `preparedByPrincipalId` at approvals.ts:87. Producers to fix in the same change, named: apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/[id]/page.tsx, apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/page.tsx, apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts and the finance/calendar call sites that build an ApprovalView. Then add `model ConflictDeclaration` and `model Recusal` (principalId, resourceId or resourceType scope, declaredAt, effectiveFrom/Until, reason) and replace `NO_STANDING_DECLARATIONS` at approvals.ts:61 with a loader that reads them for this principal and this request and builds the real `ControlWorld`. TEST (apps/web/src/lib/approvals.test.ts): a decider who prepared but did not raise the request gets SAME_MAKER and `availableActions` returns no approve/reject; a decider with an in-window recusal on this resource gets RECUSED; the same recusal dated in the past changes nothing. MUTATION TO PROVE: revert approvals.ts:87 to omit `preparedByPrincipalId` and confirm the SAME_MAKER test reds (the preparer is handed the gate again); restore. Assert through `availableActions`, the function the page and actions.ts actually call, not through `mayDecide` directly.

title: The outbox has a producer but no dispatcher, no dead-letter operator path and no inbox — dispatchOnce and replay have zero production callers
why_open: The producer half is genuinely done: apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:154 and :436 write `outboxEventRow(...)` INSIDE the deciding transaction, and the table is real (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1088-1119, migration 20260801210840_outbox_events). The consuming half is entirely unreached. `OutboxPorts` (apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:86-111), `dispatchOnce` (:140), `MAX_ATTEMPTS`/`backoffMs` (:116,:127) and `replay` (:212) are referenced nowhere outside apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.test.ts — grep across apps/web/src finds no implementation of OutboxPorts or ReplayPorts and no route or job that calls either, so no row is ever claimed, retried or dead-lettered and `state` stays 'pending' forever. There is no inbox at all: the schema has OutboxEvent and no consumed-event table, so 'idempotent consumers' has no dedupe store. OVERLAP WARNING: tools/loop/harvested-queue.json carries GE-063-005, GE-070-007 and GE-064-002 over these same files — this item must be serialized with them, not run in parallel.
smallest_real_change: 1) Add apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.ts implementing OutboxPorts over Prisma: `claimDue` does an atomic `UPDATE "OutboxEvent" SET state='dispatching' WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM "OutboxEvent" WHERE state='pending' AND "availableAt" <= $1 ORDER BY "availableAt" LIMIT $2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *` via `$queryRaw` (the @@index([state, availableAt]) at schema.prisma:1117 already serves it); markDispatched/scheduleRetry/deadLetter are plain updates. 2) Add apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts modelled exactly on apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts (same JobRequest envelope, same derived idempotencyKey at :63, same internal-header auth) whose handler calls `dispatchOnce(prismaOutboxPorts, { now })` — that is the production caller the module has never had. 3) Add `model InboxEvent { institutionId, eventId @@unique([institutionId, eventId]), consumer, consumedAt }` + migration, and have the `deliver` port record it before invoking the handler so a redelivery is a no-op — that is the 'idempotent consumer'. 4) Expose replay as an operator action over `listDead`/`requeue`, explicit ids only, as replay() at outbox.ts:212 already enforces. TEST (apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.itest.ts against the running Postgres): seed three pending rows, run the route handler, assert one pass dispatches them and a second pass claims nothing; make deliver throw and assert availableAt moves forward and attempts increments; force 8 failures and assert state='dead' with deadLetteredAt set; redeliver a dispatched eventId and assert the handler does not run twice. MUTATION TO PROVE: remove `SKIP LOCKED` (or the state predicate) from claimDue and confirm the concurrent-claim test reds with the same row claimed twice; drop the InboxEvent write and confirm the redelivery test reds.

title: Receipt capture, coding, matching and approval are already implemented end-to-end — do not rebuild
why_open: ALREADY DONE, contrary to the ledger's FAIL. Capture: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:378-405 takes a `receipt` file, requires it once storage is configured (:383), enforces a 15 MB cap (:386) and stores it as a Document. Coding: the submitter picks the budget line and category (same action, apps/web/src/components/finance/ReimbursementForm.tsx). Matching: apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:309-310 and :330-377 post the SPEND linked to BOTH the approval and the receipt document — the three-way match request-approval-receipt, deduped by the `already` lookup at :332 so a second decision cannot double-post, and using `{ increment: signed }` at :368 so two concurrent posts cannot lose one. Approval: it rides the president/OSE workflow (apps/web/src/lib/workflows/approval-definition.ts). Exceptions: apps/web/src/lib/policies.ts:331,362 encode the missing-receipt and itemization exception rules. What is genuinely missing from this requirement is only the allocation cap on the posting, which is filed separately as PAY-070-007 — an implementer should do that and mark this PASS with the citations above rather than building a second receipt pipeline.
smallest_real_change: No new implementation. Record PAY-110-005 in docs/implementation/payments-treasury-execution-ledger.md with the file:line evidence above, and add the one missing assertion to the existing suite: a test that a reimbursement submitted with no receipt while storage IS configured is refused at apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:383, and that a second final approval of the same request posts no second LedgerEntry (the `already` guard at apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:332). MUTATION TO PROVE: delete the `storageConfigured() && !hasFile` throw at :383 and confirm the first test reds; delete the `already` lookup and confirm the double-post test reds.
